key_insight: A PICNN can serve as the prediction step in a physics-preserving scheme for two-phase porous-media flow, while post-processing restores thermodynamic consistency, mass conservation, and bounds preservation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate for challenging flow solvers in reservoir and porous-media simulations, especially when permeability is discontinuous and flux continuity must be respected.
method: PICNN is trained on finite-volume residuals instead of standard PINN losses.
Interfacial fluxes are computed with TPFA using two-point difference quotients of neighboring cell-centered unknowns.
A correction/post-processing step enforces energy stability, mass conservation, and variable bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical results showing that the finite-volume-residual PICNN can replace the traditional prediction solver and outperform conventional PINN-style handling of local interactions.
watch_item: The approach still depends on a separate correction stage and on accurate TPFA-based flux discretization, so performance may be sensitive to mesh quality and heterogeneous coefficient fields.
paper_title: The PICNN-Assisted Physics-Preserving Scheme for Thermodynamically Consistent Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media
